brief: A working Great Lakes shipyard on the bay (Bay Shipbuilding, formed 1968; the yard's big sheds and cranes date from the 1970s on): tall grey steel fabrication halls, gantry and crawler cranes, and lake freighters laid up at the quay for winter repair. Two photos. Scaled down to the lot. Quay piles 10 m below the bed (spec rule 4).

facade.notes: Bay Shipbuilding (Sturgeon Bay WI), seen from across the bay: a very tall grey metal fabrication hall with a white end, lattice crawler cranes, two thousand-foot lake freighters at the fitting-out wall; flat calm water

why.note: a shipyard: one huge tall hall for building hull blocks, cranes along the fitting-out wall and a graving dock
